notes: Named palettes a masjid can pick instead of the one derived from its theme_settings. Colours here are inputs to palette.js resolvePalette(), which re-checks every ink against WCAG AA before it reaches a template — a hand-added palette cannot ship an unreadable disclaimer.

burlington-purple.name: Burlington Purple
burlington-purple.note: Sampled down the centre of 19 exemplars, agreeing to within a couple of values. This is Burlington's brand, not the product's — it is the default for masjid 1 and is not offered to other tenants.

cool-neutral.name: Cool Neutral
cool-neutral.note: The product default: a blue-grey ground that flatters a photographed dish without claiming a brand.

sage-mist.name: Sage Mist
sage-mist.note: Cool green. The nearest neutral to a masjid whose brand is already green.

slate-dawn.name: Slate Dawn
slate-dawn.note: Coldest of the set. Highest contrast under the disclaimer, so it is the safe pick when a flyer runs long.

sand-warm.name: Warm Sand
sand-warm.note: The one warm option. Offered because food photography often reads better on it — pick deliberately, it is not the default.

janazah-night.name: Janazah Night
janazah-night.note: Solid, no gradient. The janazah template reads --flyer-ground only; the grad stops are present so the same palette object shape works everywhere.
